answers.rationale: The open-jaw options, a Boise round trip with backtracking, and driving for mileage can each be preferable depending on airfares, one-way rental drop charges, reimbursable mileage rate, flight times, and rules for transporting the boxes. None of those criteria is given.
A Boston round trip avoids a one-way rental fee, while the open-jaw plans reduce backtracking; the relative airfare, rental terms, airport schedules, and acceptable driving time are unspecified.

Charlotte and Greensboro arrivals, plus either an Asheville open jaw or a return to the origin airport, are viable shells under different fare, rental-drop-fee, driving-time, and flight-schedule assumptions. The query provides no basis to choose among them.

A Tuesday arrival minimizes an extra hotel night, while either Monday arrival provides different amounts of buffer before the first session. The applicable reliability, cost, work-time, and arrival-buffer preferences are not stated.

The Saturday nonstop meets the stated event, but Friday arrivals may be preferred for buffer time, family time, or airfare reasons. There is no stated policy or preference that makes either same-day or prior-day travel uniquely correct.

Sunday morning travel is workable and reduces an overnight stay, while either Saturday option adds buffer before speaker preparation. Flight reliability, cost, required preparation time, and arrival preferences are absent.

Transit and rideshares may be sufficient, but a rental for the dinner or full stay may be better depending on the dinner location, transit service, parking, rental cost, and accessibility needs. Those details are not supplied.

Rail plus rideshare is a reasonable plan, but a rental can also be reasonable if the dinner location, timing, parking arrangement, transit access, or traveler requirements make it advantageous. The query does not resolve those factors.

Skipping the rental or renting only for the reception can each fit the described itinerary; a full rental may also be justified by unspecified transit, parking, timing, or accessibility constraints. No cost or local-travel details select one plan uniquely.

The Sacramento/Fresno open jaw reduces backtracking, while Bay Area returns or an SFO round trip may have better schedules, fares, availability, or rental terms. The query says all routings fit but omits the criteria needed to rank them.

The conference hotel offers convenience, but airport, suburban, or outlying chain hotels could be preferable based on rates, reimbursement limits, loyalty, parking, and ground-transportation arrangements. Those deciding details are not given.

The downtown hotel minimizes travel to the listed events, but the airport, suburban, and business-park options can be preferable under different rate, parking, loyalty, transport, or personal-schedule constraints. The query does not establish a governing priority.
